```{r}
  path       = kampala_dir,

```

```{r}
stopifnot(all(geom_ok))
```

```{r}
# 2. Create a multi-layer SpatRaster
r_stack <- terra::rast(r_list)

# 3. Assign quarter labels to layers
layer_names <- gsub("ntl_|_kampala\\.tif", "", basename(files))
names(r_stack) <- gsub("_", " ", layer_names)

# 4. Extract spatial and temporal dimensions
nrow_k   <- terra::nrow(r_stack)
ncol_k   <- terra::ncol(r_stack)
n_cells  <- terra::ncell(r_stack)
T_layers <- terra::nlyr(r_stack)

# 5. Extract pixel-by-quarter matrix (without NA, matrix size is [n_cells x T_layers])
Y <- terra::values(r_stack)
```

# 2. Construction of Spatial and Temporal Penalty Matrices

`build_spatial_D()` builds the spatial fused-lasso penalty matrix D_space, connecting horizontal and vertical pixel neighbors WITHIN each quarter, replicated across all T_layers quarters.

```{r}
build_spatial_D <- function(r_stack, nrow_k, ncol_k, n_cells, T_layers) {
  
  ## Horizontal edges (right neighbor), for ONE quarter
  rows_h <- rep(1:nrow_k, each = ncol_k - 1)
  cols_h <- rep(1:(ncol_k - 1), times = nrow_k)
  
  cell_left  <- terra::cellFromRowCol(r_stack, rows_h, cols_h)
  cell_right <- terra::cellFromRowCol(r_stack, rows_h, cols_h + 1)
  n_h <- length(cell_left)
  
  ## Vertical edges (bottom neighbor), for ONE quarter
  rows_v <- rep(1:(nrow_k - 1), each = ncol_k)
  cols_v <- rep(1:ncol_k, times = nrow_k - 1)
  
  cell_top    <- terra::cellFromRowCol(r_stack, rows_v, cols_v)
  cell_bottom <- terra::cellFromRowCol(r_stack, rows_v + 1, cols_v)
  n_v <- length(cell_top)
  
  ## Assemble edge list for a SINGLE quarter (local cell indices)
  n_spatial_edges_per_quarter <- n_h + n_v
  
  i_h <- rep(1:n_h, each = 2)
  j_h <- as.vector(rbind(cell_left, cell_right))
  x_h <- rep(c(1, -1), times = n_h)
  
  i_v <- rep(n_h + (1:n_v), each = 2)
  j_v <- as.vector(rbind(cell_top, cell_bottom))
  x_v <- rep(c(1, -1), times = n_v)
  
  i_base <- c(i_h, i_v)
  j_base <- c(j_h, j_v)
  x_base <- c(x_h, x_v)
  
  ## Replicate the single-quarter edge list across all T_layers quarters
  i_full <- unlist(lapply(1:T_layers, function(t) i_base + (t - 1) * n_spatial_edges_per_quarter))
  j_full <- unlist(lapply(1:T_layers, function(t) j_base + (t - 1) * n_cells))
  x_full <- rep(x_base, T_layers)
  
  n_spatial_edges <- n_spatial_edges_per_quarter * T_layers
  
  D_space <- sparseMatrix(i = i_full, j = j_full, x = x_full,
                          dims = c(n_spatial_edges, n_cells * T_layers))
  
  ## sanity check: independent formula for the expected edge count
  expected_edges <- (nrow_k * (ncol_k - 1) + (nrow_k - 1) * ncol_k) * T_layers
  stopifnot(nrow(D_space) == expected_edges)
  
  D_space
}
```

`build_temporal_D()` builds the temporal fused-lasso penalty matrix D_time, connecting each pixel to itself in the next quarter (t -\> t+1).

```{r}
build_temporal_D <- function(n_cells, T_layers) {
  
  n_temporal_edges <- n_cells * (T_layers - 1)
  
  # pixel id, repeated per transition
  cell_seq <- rep(1:n_cells, times = T_layers - 1)          
  # source quarter of the transition
  t_seq <- rep(1:(T_layers - 1), each = n_cells)         
  
  idx_t1 <- (t_seq - 1) * n_cells + cell_seq # global index at time t
  idx_t2 <- t_seq * n_cells + cell_seq # global index at time t+1
  
  t_i <- rep(1:n_temporal_edges, each = 2)
  t_j <- as.vector(rbind(idx_t1, idx_t2))
  t_x <- rep(c(1, -1), times = n_temporal_edges)
  
  D_time <- sparseMatrix(i = t_i, j = t_j, x = t_x,
                         dims = c(n_temporal_edges, n_cells * T_layers))
  
  stopifnot(nrow(D_time) == n_temporal_edges)
  
  D_time
}
```

```{r}
# Usage
D_space <- build_spatial_D(r_stack, nrow_k, ncol_k, n_cells, T_layers)
D_time  <- build_temporal_D(n_cells, T_layers)

# Sanity checks
expected_p <- n_cells * T_layers
beta <- numeric(expected_p)

stopifnot(ncol(D_time) == expected_p)
stopifnot(ncol(D_space) == expected_p)
stopifnot(length(beta) == expected_p)

cat(sprintf("D_space: %d spatial edges x %d coefficients\n", nrow(D_space), ncol(D_space)))
cat(sprintf("D_time:  %d temporal edges x %d coefficients\n", nrow(D_time), ncol(D_time)))
```

```{r}
n_h <- nrow_k * (ncol_k - 1)   # horizontal edges in one quarter
n_v <- (nrow_k - 1) * ncol_k   # vertical edges in one quarter

D_space_q1 <- D_space[1:(n_h + n_v), 1:n_cells, drop = FALSE]

# Extract the non-zero entries directly, no dense conversion needed
D_summary <- summary(D_space_q1)   # data.frame with columns i, j, x

# 1. each edge (row of D) must have exactly two non-zero entries
counts_per_row <- table(D_summary$i)
stopifnot(all(counts_per_row == 2))

# 2. the two entries must be +1 and -1 (they must cancel out)
sums_per_row <- tapply(D_summary$x, D_summary$i, sum)
stopifnot(all(sums_per_row == 0))

# 3. the two connected pixels must be actual grid neighbors (Manhattan distance 1)
cols_per_row <- split(D_summary$j, D_summary$i) # list: one vector of 2 column indices per edge
cols_mat <- do.call(rbind, cols_per_row) # matrix: n_edges x 2

to_rc <- function(idx) cbind(row = ceiling(idx / ncol_k),
                             col = ((idx - 1) %% ncol_k) + 1)
rc1 <- to_rc(cols_mat[, 1])
rc2 <- to_rc(cols_mat[, 2])

manhattan_dist <- abs(rc1[, "row"] - rc2[, "row"]) + abs(rc1[, "col"] - rc2[, "col"])
stopifnot(all(manhattan_dist == 1))

cat("D_space_q1: structure verified -", nrow(D_space_q1), "edges, all between valid neighbors\n")
```

## Validation test: compare D_space (single quarter) against genlasso's own D2d construction, without running any solver

**Structural Validation of the Spatial Adjacency Matrix (D_space)**

Each row of $D_{space}$ represents a single edge in the spatial adjacency graph, which is a pair of pixels that the fused lasso penalty tries to fuse together. Rather than trusting the construction blindly, this check verifies three properties that must hold if the matrix is correct.

- **First,** the validation checks that every row has exactly two non-zero entries. Since a row encodes a difference between two pixels, it must involve exactly two columns, specifically one for each pixel in the pair. Using `summary()` on the sparse matrix gives only the non-zero positions directly, without ever densifying the matrix, and counting how many times each row index appears determines whether any edge is malformed, such as a pixel connected to itself, or a corrupted row with too few or too many entries.

- **Second,** the validation checks that the two non-zero values in each row sum to zero. Since a row represents $\beta_a - \beta_b$, the two entries should be $+1$ and $-1$. Rather than checking each value individually, summing them provides a fast, vectorized way to confirm the correct signs, because if they summed to anything other than zero, it would indicate a sign bug in the construction.

The first two checks only validate the shape of each row (two entries with opposite signs), leaving open the question of which pixels are actually connected. A row could technically have two valid $+1/-1$ entries linking two pixels on opposite corners of the grid, and these two checks alone would not catch it.

- **Third,** the process converts each pixel's linear column index back into its $(row, column)$ position on the grid, which is the inverse of the indexing formula used to build $D_{space}$ initially, and computes the Manhattan distance between the two pixels in each edge by taking the sum of the absolute differences in row and column. A distance of exactly $1$ confirms the two pixels are true grid neighbors (up, down, left, or right), a distance of $0$ indicates a pixel connected to itself, and anything greater than $1$ means the edge links non-adjacent pixels, revealing a bug capable of slipping silently into complex indexing, such as gluing together pixels from different quarters due to incorrect offsets.

Taken together, the first two checks confirm that each row is well-formed as a difference term, while the third confirms meaningful construction, ensuring the matrix genuinely encodes physical adjacency on the pixel grid, which is the property that establishes $D_{space}$ as a spatial penalty rather than an arbitrary set of connections.

```{r}
## -------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Extract the single-quarter block from the full D_space
## -------------------------------------------------------------
n_h <- nrow_k * (ncol_k - 1)
n_v <- (nrow_k - 1) * ncol_k
D_space_q1 <- D_space[1:(n_h + n_v), 1:n_cells, drop = FALSE]

## -------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Get genlasso's own spatial penalty matrix directly
##    (fusedlasso2d() builds D internally exactly this way)
## -------------------------------------------------------------
D_genlasso <- getD2dSparse(nrow_k, ncol_k)

## -------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Structural checks on D_space_q1
## -------------------------------------------------------------
D_summary <- summary(D_space_q1)   # sparse triplet: columns i, j, x

# each edge (row of D) must have exactly two non-zero entries
counts_per_row <- table(D_summary$i)
stopifnot(all(counts_per_row == 2))

# the two entries must be +1 and -1 (they must cancel out)
sums_per_row <- tapply(D_summary$x, D_summary$i, sum)
stopifnot(all(sums_per_row == 0))

# the two connected pixels must be actual grid neighbors (Manhattan distance 1)
cols_per_row <- split(D_summary$j, D_summary$i)
cols_mat <- do.call(rbind, cols_per_row)

to_rc <- function(idx) cbind(row = ceiling(idx / ncol_k),
                             col = ((idx - 1) %% ncol_k) + 1)
rc1 <- to_rc(cols_mat[, 1])
rc2 <- to_rc(cols_mat[, 2])

manhattan_dist <- abs(rc1[, "row"] - rc2[, "row"]) + abs(rc1[, "col"] - rc2[, "col"])
stopifnot(all(manhattan_dist == 1))

cat(sprintf("D_space_q1: structure verified - %d edges, all between valid neighbors\n",
            nrow(D_space_q1)))

## -------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Same edge count as genlasso's own D2d?
## -------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(nrow(D_genlasso) == n_h + n_v)
stopifnot(nrow(D_genlasso) == nrow(D_space_q1))

## -------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Compare the actual edge sets between the two matrices
##
## NOTE: terra (used to build D_space) and genlasso's getD2dSparse
## use different pixel indexing conventions:
##   - terra::cellFromRowCol() is row-major: index = (row-1)*ncol + col
##   - genlasso follows R's standard column-major convention:
##     index = row + (col-1)*dim1
## Same underlying grid graph, different node labels. Indices are
## translated into genlasso's convention before comparing.
## -------------------------------------------------------------
r_vec <- rep(1:nrow_k, each = ncol_k)
c_vec <- rep(1:ncol_k, times = nrow_k)

idx_genlasso_vec <- r_vec + (c_vec - 1) * nrow_k # same pixels, genlasso-style index
terra_to_genlasso <- idx_genlasso_vec # lookup table: terra index -> genlasso index

# Remap D_space_q1's column indices into genlasso's indexing convention
D_summary$j_mapped <- terra_to_genlasso[D_summary$j]

edges_mine_mapped <- sapply(split(D_summary$j_mapped, D_summary$i), function(cols) {
  paste(sort(cols), collapse = "-")
})

genlasso_summary <- summary(D_genlasso)
edges_genlasso <- sapply(split(genlasso_summary$j, genlasso_summary$i), function(cols) {
  paste(sort(cols), collapse = "-")
})

edges_match <- setequal(edges_mine_mapped, edges_genlasso)
cat(sprintf("Edge sets match genlasso's D2d (after index translation): %s\n", edges_match))

stopifnot(edges_match)
cat("D_space_q1 is confirmed equivalent to genlasso::getD2dSparse()\n")
```

# 3. Formulation and Solution of the Spatiotemporal Fused Lasso Optimization Problem

Idea: Capture both spatial smoothness and temporal trends simultaneously $\to$ extend standard 1D trend filtering and 2D fused lasso into a unified **3D Spatiotemporal Fused Lasso** framework

Given a spatio-temporal dataset where $y_{s,t}$ represents the observed value at spatial location (pixel) $s \in \{1, \dots, S\}$ and time step $t \in \{1, \dots, T\}$, the optimal regularized coefficient matrix $\hat{\beta}$ is defined as the solution to the following convex optimization problem:

$$\hat{\beta} = \arg\min_{\beta} \left\{ \frac{1}{2} \sum_{s=1}^{S} \sum_{t=1}^{T} (y_{s,t} - \beta_{s,t})^2 + \lambda_1 \sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{(s,s') \in \mathcal{E}} \vert{}\beta_{s,t} - \beta_{s',t}\vert{} + \lambda_2 \sum_{s=1}^{S} \sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \vert{}\beta_{s,t} - \beta_{s,t+1}\vert{} \right\}$$

## Breakdown of the Objective Function

The formulation consists of three primary components:

- **Data Fidelity Term (**$\frac{1}{2} \sum \sum (y_{s,t} - \beta_{s,t})^2$):

  This term measures the Residual Sum of Squares (RSS) between the raw observations $y_{s,t}$ and the estimated spatio-temporal coefficients $\beta_{s,t}$, ensuring that the fitted model remains faithful to the original data.

- **Spatial Penalty Term (**$\lambda_1 \sum \sum \vert{}\beta_{s,t} - \beta_{s',t}\vert{}$):

  Controlled by the tuning parameter $\lambda_1 \ge 0$, this component computes the $L_1$-norm of the differences between neighboring pixels. Here, $\mathcal{E}$ denotes the set of spatial edges (adjacent pixel pairs on the 2D grid). This encourages spatial piece-wise constancy, grouping neighboring pixels with similar characteristics into homogeneous spatial regions for any given time step $t$.

- **Temporal Penalty Term (**$\lambda_2 \sum \sum \vert{}\beta_{s,t} - \beta_{s,t+1}\vert{}$):

  Controlled by the tuning parameter $\lambda_2 \ge 0$, this component acts as a 0-th order trend filter over time. It penalizes abrupt changes between consecutive time steps for each individual pixel $s$, enforcing a piece-wise constant temporal trajectory (step-like behavior).

Solved via ADMM (Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers) - 2 independent lambdas, no path algorithm, sparse Cholesky factorized once and reused across iterations)

```{r}
# soft_threshold()
# Proximal operator of the L1 norm: S_t(x) = sign(x) * max(|x|-t, 0)
soft_threshold <- function(x, t) {
  sign(x) * pmax(abs(x) - t, 0)
}
```

`prepare_admm_operators()` = Precomputes everything that does NOT depend on lambda1/lambda2: sparse D matrices and the Cholesky factorization of M, which only depends on rho. Reused across the entire lambda grid.

```{r}
prepare_admm_operators <- function(D_space, D_time, n, rho) {
  D_s <- as(D_space, "CsparseMatrix")
  D_t <- as(D_time,  "CsparseMatrix")
  I_n <- Diagonal(n)
  
  M <- I_n + rho * (crossprod(D_s) + crossprod(D_t))
  M <- as(M, "CsparseMatrix")
  chol_M <- Cholesky(M, LDL = FALSE, super = TRUE)
  
  list(D_s = D_s, D_t = D_t, chol_M = chol_M,
       n = n, ms = nrow(D_space), mt = nrow(D_time), rho = rho)
}
```

```{r}
# admm_fusedlasso3d()
# y        : observed vector, length n = n_cells * T_layers
# ops      : precomputed operators from prepare_admm_operators()
# lambda1  : spatial fusion penalty
# lambda2  : temporal fusion penalty
admm_fusedlasso3d <- function(y, ops, lambda1, lambda2,
                              max_iter = 500,
                              tol_abs = 1e-4,
                              tol_rel = 1e-3,
                              verbose = TRUE) {
  
  n <- ops$n; ms <- ops$ms; mt <- ops$mt; rho <- ops$rho
  D_s <- ops$D_s; D_t <- ops$D_t; chol_M <- ops$chol_M
  
  ## Initialization
  beta <- y
  z1 <- as.numeric(D_s %*% beta); u1 <- rep(0, ms)
  z2 <- as.numeric(D_t %*% beta); u2 <- rep(0, mt)
  
  history <- data.frame(iter = integer(), r_norm = double(), s_norm = double())
  
  for (k in seq_len(max_iter)) {
    
    ## beta-update
    rhs <- y +
      rho * as.numeric(crossprod(D_s, z1 - u1)) +
      rho * as.numeric(crossprod(D_t, z2 - u2))
    beta <- as.numeric(solve(chol_M, rhs))
    
    Ds_beta <- as.numeric(D_s %*% beta)
    Dt_beta <- as.numeric(D_t %*% beta)
    
    ## z-update (soft-threshold)
    z1_old <- z1; z2_old <- z2
    z1 <- soft_threshold(Ds_beta + u1, lambda1 / rho)
    z2 <- soft_threshold(Dt_beta + u2, lambda2 / rho)
    
    ## dual update
    u1 <- u1 + Ds_beta - z1
    u2 <- u2 + Dt_beta - z2
    
    ## Stopping criteria (Boyd et al. 2011)
    r_norm <- sqrt(sum((Ds_beta - z1)^2) + sum((Dt_beta - z2)^2))
    
    s_vec  <- rho * (as.numeric(crossprod(D_s, z1 - z1_old)) + as.numeric(crossprod(D_t, z2 - z2_old)))
    s_norm <- sqrt(sum(s_vec^2))
    
    eps_pri  <- sqrt(ms + mt) * tol_abs +
      tol_rel * max(sqrt(sum(Ds_beta^2) + sum(Dt_beta^2)),
                    sqrt(sum(z1^2) + sum(z2^2)))
    
    dual_var_term <- rho * (as.numeric(crossprod(D_s, u1)) + as.numeric(crossprod(D_t, u2)))
    eps_dual <- sqrt(n) * tol_abs + tol_rel * sqrt(sum(dual_var_term^2))
    
    history <- rbind(history, data.frame(iter = k, r_norm = r_norm, s_norm = s_norm))
    
    if (verbose && (k %% 25 == 0)) {
      cat(sprintf("iter %4d | primal res = %.6f | dual res = %.6f\n", k, r_norm, s_norm))
    }
    
    if (r_norm < eps_pri && s_norm < eps_dual) {
      if (verbose) cat(sprintf("Converged at iteration %d\n", k))
      break
    }
  }
  
  list(beta = beta, z1 = z1, z2 = z2,
       u1 = u1, u2 = u2,
       history = history, n_iter = k)
}
```

# Lambda grid search (BIC-based)

`build_lambda_grid()` = Log-spaced grid of lambda values, denser near zero (absolute gaps shrink automatically at the low end under log spacing), with 0 included explicitly as the no-penalty case.

```{r}
build_lambda_grid <- function(min_val = 1e-3, max_val = 5, n = 15) {
  c(0, exp(seq(log(min_val), log(max_val), length.out = n)))
}
```

## Noise Variance Estimator ($\hat{\sigma}^2$)

To evaluate model performance and compute scale-free information criteria (such as scaled BIC), two alternative strategies for estimating the global noise variance $\hat{\sigma}^2$ in the 3D Spatio-Temporal Fused Lasso are available.

`estimate_sigma2()` = Global noise variance estimate for the 3D model.

The estimate is computed once from the raw data and is the same for every pair $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2)$ of the grid.

### Option 1: Graph-Based First-Difference Estimator (Rice-type)

It applies a Rice-type first-difference estimator ($\text{Var(diff)} = 2\sigma^2$ under a slowly-varying signal and uncorrelated noise) to all the edges of the spatio-temporal graph, pooling the spatial and the temporal first differences of the raw observed data: $$
\hat{\sigma}^2 = \frac{1}{2}\,\text{mean}\left(\left[ D_{\text{space}}\, y ;\; D_{\text{time}}\, y \right]^2\right) = \frac{\lVert D_{\text{space}}\, y \rVert_2^2 + \lVert D_{\text{time}}\, y \rVert_2^2}{2\,(m_1 + m_2)}
$$where $m_1$ and $m_2$ denote the total numbers of spatial and temporal edges, respectively. Since the mean is computed globally across the entire pooled vector, each direction is implicitly weighted by its respective structural cardinality.

Note on Edge Proportions: In a regular 3D spatio-temporal grid ($S$ spatial pixels observed over $T$ time periods), the spatial penalty matrix $D_{\text{space}}$ accounts for horizontal and vertical adjacencies across all $T$ layers ($\approx 2ST$ edges), while the temporal penalty matrix $D_{\text{time}}$ tracks the single temporal transition for each pixel ($S(T-1) \approx ST$ edges). Consequently, pooling all differences assigns roughly 66% of the weight to the spatial dimensions and 34% to the temporal dimension, reflecting the natural 2D-to-1D topological imbalance of space-time graphs.

```{r}
estimate_sigma2_1st <- function(y, D_space, D_time) {
  diffs <- c(as.numeric(D_space %*% y), as.numeric(D_time %*% y))
  sig2 <- mean(diffs^2) / 2
  if (!is.finite(sig2) || sig2 <= 0) sig2 <- 1e-6
  sig2
}

# Example execution
y <- as.vector(Y)
estimate_sigma2_1st(y, D_space, D_time)
```

### Option 2: Directional Second-Difference Estimator (Tensor Array)

Alternatively, second-order differences filter out local linear trends across space and time. For a 1D second difference, $\operatorname{Var}(\Delta^{(2)} y) = 6\sigma^2$. Summing the average squared second differences across horizontal, vertical, and temporal dimensions yields $18\sigma^2$, leading to the unbiased estimator:

$$
\hat{\sigma}^2 = \frac{\text{mean}(d_h^2) + \text{mean}(d_v^2) + \text{mean}(d_t^2)}{18}
$$

```{r}
dims <- c(nrow_k, ncol_k, T_layers)
dims
```

```{r}
estimate_sigma2_2nd <- function(y, dims) {
  A  <- aperm(array(y, dim = dims[c(2, 1, 3)]), c(2, 1, 3)) # [row, column, quarter]
  dh <- A[, 3:dims[2], ] - 2 * A[, 2:(dims[2] - 1), ] + A[, 1:(dims[2] - 2), ]
  dv <- A[3:dims[1], , ] - 2 * A[2:(dims[1] - 1), , ] + A[1:(dims[1] - 2), , ]
  dt <- A[, , 3:dims[3]] - 2 * A[, , 2:(dims[3] - 1)] + A[, , 1:(dims[3] - 2)]
  sig2 <- (mean(dh^2) + mean(dv^2) + mean(dt^2)) / 18
  if (!is.finite(sig2) || sig2 <= 0) sig2 <- 1e-6
  sig2
}

# Example execution
estimate_sigma2_2nd(y, dims)
```

`get_edge_pairs()` = Precomputes the (pixel_a, pixel_b) lookup table for every edge in a penalty matrix, ONCE. This topology never changes across lambda values, only which edges end up fused does.

```{r}
get_edge_pairs <- function(D) {
  s <- summary(D)
  s <- s[order(s$i), ]
  matrix(s$j, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
}
```

`compute_df()` = Degrees of freedom estimate: number of connected components of the pixel graph after keeping only fused edges (estimated difference equal to zero). Uses precomputed edge pair tables, no rebuilding.

```{r}
compute_df <- function(z1, z2, edge_pairs_space, edge_pairs_time, n, tol = 1e-8) {
  el_space <- edge_pairs_space[abs(z1) < tol, , drop = FALSE]
  el_time  <- edge_pairs_time[abs(z2) < tol, , drop = FALSE]
  el <- rbind(el_space, el_time)
  
  if (nrow(el) == 0) return(n)   # no fusion at all: every pixel is its own component
  
  g <- graph_from_edgelist(el, directed = FALSE)
  g <- add_vertices(g, n - vcount(g))
  components(g)$no
}
```

`snap_beta_to_clusters()` = ADMM converges to D\*beta = z only asymptotically, so a finite number of iterations always leaves a residual gap between the two, even for edges the auxiliary variable z has already fused to zero. This function removes that gap explicitly: pixels belonging to the same fused connected component (`z == 0`) are forced to share the exact same value, using the cluster mean of beta (the least-squares-optimal constant for that group).

```{r}
snap_beta_to_clusters <- function(beta, z1, z2, edge_pairs_space, edge_pairs_time, n, tol = 1e-8) {
  el_space <- edge_pairs_space[abs(z1) < tol, , drop = FALSE]
  el_time  <- edge_pairs_time[abs(z2) < tol, , drop = FALSE]
  el <- rbind(el_space, el_time)
  
  if (nrow(el) == 0) return(beta)   # no fusion: nothing to snap
  
  g <- graph_from_edgelist(el, directed = FALSE)
  g <- add_vertices(g, n - vcount(g))
  cluster_id <- components(g)$membership
  
  ave(beta, cluster_id)
}
```

`setup_cluster()` = Creates a PSOCK cluster and has each worker factorize its own Cholesky decomposition ONCE, so the (potentially large) factorization is never transferred over clusterExport(). Reuse the returned cluster across multiple `grid_search_lambda()` calls to amortize this setup cost.

```{r}
setup_cluster <- function(n_cores, D_space, D_time, n, rho) {
  cl <- parallel::makeCluster(n_cores)
  
  parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, { library(Matrix); library(igraph) })
  parallel::clusterExport(cl,
                          varlist = c("D_space", "D_time", "n", "rho",
                                      "prepare_admm_operators", "admm_fusedlasso3d",
                                      "soft_threshold", "compute_df",
                                      "snap_beta_to_clusters"),
                          envir = environment())
  
  parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, {
    ops <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space, D_time, n, rho)
  })
  
  cl
}
```

`grid_search_lambda()` = Fits the ADMM model over a grid of (lambda1, lambda2) combinations. Edge topology is precomputed once; combinations can optionally be evaluated in parallel across cores by passing an already-prepared PSOCK cluster (see `setup_cluster()`, Windows-compatible), which amortizes Cholesky factorization and worker startup cost across multiple grid searches instead of repeating it on every call.

```{r}
# grid_search_lambda() - Option 2 (Tensor Second-Differences / 18)
# y            : observed vector, length n
# dims         : dimensions vector c(nrow, ncol, T_layers) for the 3D tensor array (needed for estimate_sigma2_2nd)
# D_space      : spatial penalty matrix (needed for edge topology, 
#                even when reusing an externally prepared cluster)
# D_time       : temporal penalty matrix
# lambda1_grid : grid of spatial fusion penalties
# lambda2_grid : grid of temporal fusion penalties
# cl           : optional, already-prepared cluster from setup_cluster().
#                When supplied, the cluster is reused as-is (not created
#                or destroyed here), so its setup cost is amortized across
#                multiple grid_search_lambda() calls.
# n_cores      : used only when cl is NULL, to create and destroy a
#                cluster internally for this single call (backward-compatible)
grid_search_lambda <- function(y, dims, D_space, D_time,
                               lambda1_grid, lambda2_grid,
                               cl = NULL, rho = 1, max_iter = 300, n_cores = 1) {
  
  n <- length(y)
  sigma2_est <- estimate_sigma2_2nd(y, dims)
  
  edge_pairs_space <- get_edge_pairs(D_space)
  edge_pairs_time  <- get_edge_pairs(D_time)
  
  combos <- expand.grid(lambda1 = lambda1_grid, lambda2 = lambda2_grid)
  rows <- split(combos, seq_len(nrow(combos)))
  
  fit_one <- function(row) {
    fit <- admm_fusedlasso3d(y, ops, row$lambda1, row$lambda2,
                             max_iter = max_iter, verbose = FALSE)
    
    beta_snapped <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit$beta, fit$z1, fit$z2,
                                          edge_pairs_space, edge_pairs_time, n)
    
    rss <- sum((y - beta_snapped)^2)
    df  <- compute_df(fit$z1, fit$z2, edge_pairs_space, edge_pairs_time, n)
    bic <- (rss / sigma2_est) + df * log(n)
    
    data.frame(lambda1 = row$lambda1, lambda2 = row$lambda2,
               rss = rss, df = df, bic = bic)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(cl)) {
    # Reuse an externally created and already-prepared cluster
    parallel::clusterExport(cl,
                            varlist = c("y", "edge_pairs_space", "edge_pairs_time", "sigma2_est", "max_iter"),
                            envir = environment())
    
    results_list <- parallel::parLapplyLB(cl, rows, fit_one)
    
  } else if (n_cores > 1) {
    # Backward-compatible: create and destroy a cluster internally for this call
    cl_local <- setup_cluster(n_cores, D_space, D_time, n, rho)
    on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl_local), add = TRUE)
    
    parallel::clusterExport(cl_local,
                            varlist = c("y", "edge_pairs_space", "edge_pairs_time", "sigma2_est", "max_iter"),
                            envir = environment())
    
    results_list <- parallel::parLapplyLB(cl_local, rows, fit_one)
    
  } else {
    ops <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space, D_time, n, rho)
    results_list <- lapply(rows, fit_one)
  }
  
  results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  best_row <- results[which.min(results$bic), ]
  
  list(results = results, best = best_row, sigma2_est = sigma2_est)
}
```

## Run the grid search on the real Kampala data

> **Note:** grid search results are cached in `fused_lasso_fits_folder` (`grid_out_coarse.rds`) to avoid rerunning the computationally expensive search on every render of the document. If the input data or model logic change — for example `D_space`, `D_time`, `Y`, the number of quarters, `build_lambda_grid()`, or `grid_search_lambda()` itself — the cached `.rds` file will remain the old one and be silently reloaded, with no warning that it is now outdated. In such cases, manually delete the file (or the entire `fused_lasso_fits_folder` directory) before re-running the document, to force a fresh computation.

```{r}
# Define and create the model-specific subfolder within the main fits directory
fused_lasso_fits_folder <- file.path(model_output_folder, "FusedLasso3D")

if (!dir.exists(fused_lasso_fits_folder)) {
  dir.create(fused_lasso_fits_folder)
}
```

### 1. Coarse Grid

```{r}
## Run on the real Kampala data (or load cached result if available)
y <- as.vector(Y)   # from terra::values(r_stack), part 1

lambda1_grid <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = 1e-3, max_val = 5, n = 15)
lambda2_grid <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = 1e-3, max_val = 5, n = 15)

grid_out_path <- file.path(fused_lasso_fits_folder, "grid_out_coarse_2nd.rds")

if (file.exists(grid_out_path)) {
  
  grid_out <- readRDS(grid_out_path)
  cat("Loaded cached grid search result from disk.\n")
  
} else {
  
  n_cores_to_use <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
  cl <- setup_cluster(n_cores_to_use, D_space, D_time, n = length(y), rho = 1)
  
  system.time(
    grid_out <- grid_search_lambda(
      y = y, dims = dims, D_space = D_space, D_time = D_time,
      lambda1_grid = lambda1_grid, lambda2_grid = lambda2_grid,
      cl = cl
    )
  )
  
  parallel::stopCluster(cl)
  saveRDS(grid_out, grid_out_path)
}
```

### 2. Refined Grid

```{r}
# Find the neighboring grid values around the best point, to define
# the range for the refined search (avoids picking bounds by hand)
get_refined_bounds <- function(grid, best_val) {
  sorted_grid <- sort(grid)
  idx <- which(sorted_grid == best_val)
  lower <- if (idx > 1) sorted_grid[idx - 1] else sorted_grid[idx] / 2
  upper <- if (idx < length(sorted_grid)) sorted_grid[idx + 1] else sorted_grid[idx] * 2
  c(lower, upper)
}

lambda1_bounds <- get_refined_bounds(lambda1_grid, grid_out$best$lambda1)
lambda2_bounds <- get_refined_bounds(lambda2_grid, grid_out$best$lambda2)

lambda1_grid_refined <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = lambda1_bounds[1],
                                          max_val = lambda1_bounds[2], n = 15)
lambda2_grid_refined <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = lambda2_bounds[1],
                                          max_val = lambda2_bounds[2], n = 15)

grid_out_refined_path <- file.path(fused_lasso_fits_folder, "grid_out_refined_2nd.rds")

if (file.exists(grid_out_refined_path)) {
  
  grid_out_refined <- readRDS(grid_out_refined_path)
  cat("Loaded cached refined grid search result from disk.\n")
  
} else {
  
  n_cores_to_use <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
  cl <- setup_cluster(n_cores_to_use, D_space, D_time, n = length(y), rho = 1)
  
  system.time(
    grid_out_refined <- grid_search_lambda(
      y = y, dims = dims, D_space = D_space, D_time = D_time,
      lambda1_grid = lambda1_grid_refined, lambda2_grid = lambda2_grid_refined,
      cl = cl
    )
  )
  
  parallel::stopCluster(cl)
  saveRDS(grid_out_refined, grid_out_refined_path)
}
```

## Three-Dimensional Visualization of the BIC Surface

```{r}
plot_bic_3d <- function(grid_out, plot_title) {
  df_3d <- grid_out$results[grid_out$results$lambda1 > 0 & grid_out$results$lambda2 > 0, ]
  bic_mat <- xtabs(bic ~ lambda1 + lambda2, data = df_3d)
  x_vals <- as.numeric(rownames(bic_mat))
  y_vals <- as.numeric(colnames(bic_mat))
  opt_l1 <- grid_out$best$lambda1
  opt_l2 <- grid_out$best$lambda2
  opt_bic <- grid_out$best$bic
  
  par(mfrow = c(1, 4), mar = c(1.5, 1.5, 2.5, 0.2),
      oma = c(0, 0, 3, 0), cex = 1.0)
  
  angles <- list(
    list(theta = 30, phi = 30, title = "View 1 (30°, 30°)"),
    list(theta = 120, phi = 30, title = "View 2 (120°, 30°)"),
    list(theta = 210, phi = 30, title = "View 3 (210°, 30°)"),
    list(theta = 300, phi = 30, title = "View 4 (300°, 30°)")
  )
  
  for (ang in angles) {
    res_persp <- persp(log(x_vals), log(y_vals), as.matrix(bic_mat),
                       theta = ang$theta, phi = ang$phi, expand = 0.85,
                       col = "lightblue", shade = 0.4, border = "gray80",
                       box = TRUE, ticktype = "simple",
                       xlab = "log(lambda1)",
                       ylab = "log(lambda2)",
                       zlab = "BIC",
                       main = ang$title, cex.main = 1.3, cex.lab = 1)
    
    pt <- trans3d(log(opt_l1), log(opt_l2), opt_bic, res_persp)
    points(pt$x, pt$y, col = "red", pch = 19, cex = 1.5)
    
    text_x <- pt$x
    text_y <- pt$y + 0.38
    
    par(xpd = TRUE)
    segments(pt$x, pt$y, text_x, text_y, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
    text(text_x, text_y, labels = "Min BIC", col = "red", cex = 1.1, font = 2, adj = c(0.5, 0))
    par(xpd = FALSE)
  }
  
  mtext(bquote(bold(.(plot_title) ~ "|" ~
                      "Optimal" ~ lambda[1] == .(round(opt_l1, 3)) ~ "|" ~
                      "Optimal" ~ lambda[2] == .(round(opt_l2, 3)))),
        outer = TRUE, cex = 1.5, line = 1)
  
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
```

# 4. Final Model Fit and Reconstruction of the Space-Time Signal

```{r}
cat(sprintf("Coarse:  lambda1 = %.5f, lambda2 = %.5f, BIC = %.2f\n",
            grid_out$best$lambda1, grid_out$best$lambda2, grid_out$best$bic))
cat(sprintf("Refined: lambda1 = %.5f, lambda2 = %.5f, BIC = %.2f\n",
            grid_out_refined$best$lambda1, grid_out_refined$best$lambda2,
            grid_out_refined$best$bic))
```

```{r}
## Run on the real Kampala data, using the optimal (lambda1, lambda2) found via the BIC grid search
y <- as.vector(Y)   # from terra::values(r_stack), part 1

rho <- 1
ops <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space, D_time, n = length(y), rho = rho)

fit <- admm_fusedlasso3d(
  y = y, ops = ops,
  lambda1 = grid_out_refined$best$lambda1,    # spatial fusion strength
  lambda2 = grid_out_refined$best$lambda2,    # temporal fusion strength
  max_iter = 500,
  verbose = TRUE
)

## Debias: force exact fusion within connected components, removing the
## residual gap left by ADMM's asymptotic convergence (see diagnostic above)
edge_pairs_space <- get_edge_pairs(D_space)
edge_pairs_time  <- get_edge_pairs(D_time)

beta_final <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit$beta, fit$z1, fit$z2,
                                    edge_pairs_space, edge_pairs_time, n = length(y))

## Reconstruct the estimated space-time cube from the debiased beta
beta_array <- array(beta_final, dim = c(n_cells, T_layers))

r_smoothed <- r_stack          # same geographic template
values(r_smoothed) <- beta_array
names(r_smoothed) <- names(r_stack)

## Convergence diagnostic
plot(fit$history$iter, fit$history$r_norm, type = "l", log = "y",
     xlab = "iteration", ylab = "primal residual (log scale)")
```

```{r}
for (t in seq_len(T_layers)) {
  
  # Original and smoothed raster for this quarter (both already in memory,
  # no need to reload from file or look up a per-quarter fit object)
  r_original <- r_stack[[t]]
  r_smooth   <- r_smoothed[[t]]
  
  # Scale limits computed from the original data for this quarter
  v_original <- as.numeric(terra::values(r_original))
  v_smooth   <- as.numeric(terra::values(r_smooth))
  min_val <- min(c(v_original, v_smooth), na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(c(v_original, v_smooth), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Quarter label comes from the layer name (e.g. "2013 Q1"), set in Part 1
  quarter_label <- names(r_stack)[t]
  parts <- strsplit(quarter_label, " ")[[1]]
  year    <- parts[1]
  quarter <- parts[2]
  city    <- "Kampala"
  
  bbox <- sf::st_bbox(r_original)
  x_range <- bbox["xmax"] - bbox["xmin"]
  y_range <- bbox["ymax"] - bbox["ymin"]
  pad_x <- x_range * 0.02
  pad_y <- y_range * 0.02
  
  base_style <- list(
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "viridis",
      na.value = "transparent",
      name = expression(log(NTL)),
      limits = c(min_val, max_val),
      breaks = seq(0, max_val, by = 0.5)
    ),
    coord_sf(
      xlim = c(bbox["xmin"] - pad_x, bbox["xmax"] + pad_x),
      ylim = c(bbox["ymin"] - pad_y, bbox["ymax"] + pad_y),
      expand = FALSE
    ),
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)),
    theme_minimal(),
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 18),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.5, size = 11),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.key.height = unit(2, "cm"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
    )
  )
  
  # 1. Original raster plot
  p1 <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = r_original) +
    geom_sf(data = kampala_border, fill = NA, color = "blue", linewidth = 0.6) +
    labs(title = paste0(city, " (", quarter, " ", year, ") — Original")) +
    base_style
  
  # 2. Smoothed raster plot, with the single global (lambda1, lambda2) used
  #    for the whole 3D fit (not a per-quarter value)
  p2 <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = r_smooth) +
    labs(title = bquote(bold(
      "3D Fused Lasso (" * lambda[1] * " = " * .(round(grid_out_refined$best$lambda1, 3)) *
        ", " * lambda[2] * " = " * .(round(grid_out_refined$best$lambda2, 3)) * ")"
    ))) +
    base_style
  
  shared_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(p1)
  
  p1 <- p1 + theme(legend.position = "none")
  p2 <- p2 + theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  plots_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
  
  final_grid <- cowplot::plot_grid(
    plots_combined,
    shared_legend,
    ncol = 2,
    rel_widths = c(0.90, 0.10)
  )
  
  # Output filename based on the quarter label (e.g. "FusedLasso3D_2013_Q1.png")
  file_tag <- gsub(" ", "_", quarter_label)
  plot_output_path <- file.path(fused_lasso_plots_folder, paste0("FusedLasso3D_", file_tag, ".png"))
  plot_output_path_pdf <- file.path(pdf_fused_lasso_plots_folder, paste0("FusedLasso3D_", file_tag, ".pdf"))
  
  ggsave(
    filename = plot_output_path,
    plot = final_grid,
    width = 12,
    height = 6,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )
  ggsave(
    filename = plot_output_path_pdf,
    plot = final_grid,
    width = 12,
    height = 6,
    device = "pdf",
    bg = "white"
  )
  
  print(final_grid)
}
```

## 3D Fused Lasso Output Grid

```{r}
# Function to generate a custom grid plot for the 3D Fused Lasso model
create_custom_grid_3d <- function(years_vector, 
                                  ncol_val = 8, 
                                  lambda1_val = grid_out_refined$best$lambda1,
                                  lambda2_val = grid_out_refined$best$lambda2,
                                  plot_title = NULL) {
  
  # 1. Automatic title with global lambda_1 and lambda_2 rendered via ggtext if not specified
  if (is.null(plot_title)) {
    plot_title <- paste0(
      "Kampala Nighttime Lights — 3D Fused Lasso Model Output<br>",
      "<span style='font-size:12pt; font-weight:normal;'>",
      "(<span style='font-family: serif; font-style: italic;'>&lambda;<sub>1</sub></span> = ", round(lambda1_val, 3), 
      ", <span style='font-family: serif; font-style: italic;'>&lambda;<sub>2</sub></span> = ", round(lambda2_val, 3), ")",
      "</span>"
    )
  }
  
  # 2. Filter layers from r_smoothed based on the user-specified years vector
  all_layer_names <- names(r_smoothed)
  selected_indices <- which(sapply(all_layer_names, function(lbl) {
    year_num <- as.numeric(strsplit(lbl, " ")[[1]][1])
    year_num %in% years_vector
  }))
  
  # Subset the spatio-temporal raster stack
  smooth_stack_subset <- r_smoothed[[selected_indices]]
  
  # 3. Create clean labels for each panel (e.g., "2013 Q1")
  names(smooth_stack_subset) <- all_layer_names[selected_indices]
  
  # 4. Create the ggplot object maintaining the exact 2D grid aesthetics
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = smooth_stack_subset) +
    facet_wrap(~lyr, ncol = ncol_val, strip.position = "bottom") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "viridis",
      na.value = "transparent",
      name = expression(log(NTL))
    ) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = plot_title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.spacing = unit(1, "mm"),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_markdown(size = 10, margin = margin(t = 1, b = 1.5, unit = "mm")),
      legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
      legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.title = element_markdown(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"), # element_markdown enables HTML in title
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank()
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```

## Final validation: exact fusion check on beta_final

Confirms that ADMM's asymptotic convergence gap (`Ds_beta/Dt_beta` not exactly zero on "fused" edges, as flagged during development) has been fully resolved by `snap_beta_to_clusters()`.

```{r}
Ds_beta_raw     <- as.numeric(ops$D_s %*% fit$beta)
Dt_beta_raw     <- as.numeric(ops$D_t %*% fit$beta)
Ds_beta_snapped <- as.numeric(ops$D_s %*% beta_final)
Dt_beta_snapped <- as.numeric(ops$D_t %*% beta_final)

fused_space_idx <- which(fit$z1 == 0)
fused_time_idx  <- which(fit$z2 == 0)

cat("=== Fusion check: raw ADMM beta ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Max |Ds_beta| on fused edges: %.2e\n", max(abs(Ds_beta_raw[fused_space_idx]))))
cat(sprintf("Max |Dt_beta| on fused edges: %.2e\n", max(abs(Dt_beta_raw[fused_time_idx]))))

cat("\n=== Fusion check: after snap_beta_to_clusters() ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Max |Ds_beta| on fused edges: %.2e\n", max(abs(Ds_beta_snapped[fused_space_idx]))))
cat(sprintf("Max |Dt_beta| on fused edges: %.2e\n", max(abs(Dt_beta_snapped[fused_time_idx]))))

## Hard assertion: fusion must now be exact (up to machine precision)
stopifnot(max(abs(Ds_beta_snapped[fused_space_idx])) < 1e-10)
stopifnot(max(abs(Dt_beta_snapped[fused_time_idx])) < 1e-10)

## Sanity check: snapping should be a small, consistent correction,
## not a wholesale change of the fit
mean_shift <- mean(abs(beta_final - fit$beta))
corr <- cor(fit$beta, beta_final)

cat(sprintf("\nMean |beta_final - fit$beta|: %.6f\n", mean_shift))
cat(sprintf("Correlation(fit$beta, beta_final): %.6f\n", corr))

stopifnot(corr > 0.999)   # snap should not distort the fit substantially

cat("\nAll fusion consistency checks passed.\n")
```

# Simulation Study

## TEST 1: Plus-Shaped Spatial Pattern with a Single Localized Temporal Change

Simulation: 8x8 grid, 2x2 constant blocks, 3 quarters, B = 30 Monte Carlo replications.

Ground truth: a "plus" shape on the 4x4 block grid: a center block (value 3) surrounded by its 4 neighbors (value 2) over a background (value 1). The pattern is IDENTICAL in Q1 and Q2, with a single true change in the center block at Q3 (3 -\> 5, simulating localized growth). The ground truth is fixed across replications; in each replication, independent iid Gaussian noise (sd = 0.2) is added to it.

```{r}
nrow_sim   <- 8
ncol_sim   <- 8
block_size <- 2
n_blocks   <- nrow_sim / block_size   # 4x4 blocks

sigma_sim  <- 0.2                     # noise sd
B          <- 30                      # number of Monte Carlo replications
```

`expand_blocks()` = Expands a (n_blocks x n_blocks) matrix of block-level values into the full pixel grid, repeating each value over its block_size x block_size block.

```{r}
expand_blocks <- function(block_vals, block_size) {
  block_vals[rep(1:nrow(block_vals), each = block_size),
             rep(1:ncol(block_vals), each = block_size)]
}
```

Ground truth block values (4x4 block grid), then expanded to the full 8x8 pixel grid. The truth is deterministic and shared by all replications.

```{r}
## Ground truth block values (4x4 block grid)
background_val  <- 1
neighbor_val    <- 2
center_val_q1q2 <- 3
center_val_q3   <- 5   # true change: center block grows at Q3

block_vals_q1q2 <- matrix(background_val, nrow = n_blocks, ncol = n_blocks)
block_vals_q1q2[2, 2] <- center_val_q1q2
block_vals_q1q2[1, 2] <- neighbor_val
block_vals_q1q2[3, 2] <- neighbor_val
block_vals_q1q2[2, 1] <- neighbor_val
block_vals_q1q2[2, 3] <- neighbor_val

block_vals_q3 <- block_vals_q1q2
block_vals_q3[2, 2] <- center_val_q3

## Expand to full 8x8 pixel grids
truth_q1 <- expand_blocks(block_vals_q1q2, block_size)
truth_q2 <- expand_blocks(block_vals_q1q2, block_size)   # identical to Q1
truth_q3 <- expand_blocks(block_vals_q3,   block_size)   # center block changed
```

Build the ground truth as a SpatRaster stack, so it plugs directly into the same `build_spatial_D()` / `build_temporal_D()` pipeline used on the real Kampala data. Observed stacks are not built here: noise is generated inside each replication.

```{r}
r_stack_truth <- rast(list(rast(truth_q1), rast(truth_q2), rast(truth_q3)))
names(r_stack_truth) <- c("Sim Q1", "Sim Q2", "Sim Q3")
```

Visualization: ground truth (top row) vs one example of noisy observed data (bottom row, same noise as replication b = 1), on the same color scale across all six panels for a fair comparison.

```{r}
## Example of noisy data (same noise as replication b = 1), for illustration only
truth_vec <- as.vector(terra::values(r_stack_truth))

set.seed(1000 + 1)
y_example <- truth_vec + rnorm(length(truth_vec), mean = 0, sd = sigma_sim)

r_stack_example <- r_stack_truth
values(r_stack_example) <- matrix(y_example, ncol = terra::nlyr(r_stack_truth))
names(r_stack_example) <- names(r_stack_truth)

## Same color scale across all panels
zlim_sim <- range(c(values(r_stack_truth), values(r_stack_example)), na.rm = TRUE)
zlim_sim[2] <- zlim_sim[2] + 1e-6

par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
for (t in 1:3) {
  plot(r_stack_truth[[t]], main = paste("Truth -", names(r_stack_truth)[t]),
       range = zlim_sim, type = "continuous")
}
for (t in 1:3) {
  plot(r_stack_example[[t]], main = paste("Observed (example) -", names(r_stack_example)[t]),
       range = zlim_sim, type = "continuous")
}
```

Extract the spatial/temporal dimensions and build the penalty matrices once, outside the replication loop: they depend only on the grid geometry, not on the noise. The same functions as in Part 2 (real data) are reused.

```{r}
nrow_sim_k  <- terra::nrow(r_stack_truth)
ncol_sim_k  <- terra::ncol(r_stack_truth)
n_cells_sim <- terra::ncell(r_stack_truth)
T_sim       <- terra::nlyr(r_stack_truth)

# Dimensions vector for tensor-based variance estimation (Option 2)
dims_t1 <- c(nrow_sim_k, ncol_sim_k, T_sim)

## Penalty matrices (built once, shared by all replications)
D_space_sim <- build_spatial_D(r_stack_truth, nrow_sim_k, ncol_sim_k, n_cells_sim, T_sim)
D_time_sim  <- build_temporal_D(n_cells_sim, T_sim)

cat(sprintf("Simulation built: %d x %d grid, %d quarters, noise sd = %.2f, B = %d\n",
            nrow_sim_k, ncol_sim_k, T_sim, sigma_sim, B))
cat(sprintf("D_space: %d x %d, D_time: %d x %d\n",
            nrow(D_space_sim), ncol(D_space_sim), nrow(D_time_sim), ncol(D_time_sim)))
```

Lambda grids and edge pairs, also built once outside the replication loop. Lambda grids span 1e-4 to 1 (15 values each); the upper bound was raised from 0.5 after a dry run selected lambda2 at the edge of the grid. The edge pairs are needed by `snap_beta_to_clusters()` and depend only on the penalty matrices.

```{r}
## Lambda grids (searched afresh in every replication)
lambda1_grid_sim <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = 1e-4, max_val = 1, n = 15)
lambda2_grid_sim <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = 1e-4, max_val = 1, n = 15)

## Edge pairs for the snapping step (depend only on D, not on the noise)
edge_pairs_space_sim <- get_edge_pairs(D_space_sim)
edge_pairs_time_sim  <- get_edge_pairs(D_time_sim)

cat(sprintf("Lambda grid: %d x %d = %d combinations per replication\n",
            length(lambda1_grid_sim), length(lambda2_grid_sim),
            length(lambda1_grid_sim) * length(lambda2_grid_sim)))
```

Dry run on a single replication (b = 1) to check the pipeline and measure the runtime before launching all B replications.

```{r}
b <- 1

system.time({
  set.seed(1000 + b)
  y_b <- as.vector(truth_vec + rnorm(length(truth_vec), 0, sigma_sim))
  
  grid_b <- grid_search_lambda(y = y_b, dims = dims_t1,
                               D_space = D_space_sim, D_time = D_time_sim,
                               lambda1_grid = lambda1_grid_sim,
                               lambda2_grid = lambda2_grid_sim, n_cores = 1)
  
  ops_b <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space_sim, D_time_sim, n = length(y_b), rho = 1)
  fit_b <- admm_fusedlasso3d(y = y_b, ops = ops_b,
                             lambda1 = grid_b$best$lambda1,
                             lambda2 = grid_b$best$lambda2, max_iter = 500)
  beta_b <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit_b$beta, fit_b$z1, fit_b$z2,
                                  edge_pairs_space_sim, edge_pairs_time_sim,
                                  n = length(y_b))
})

cat(sprintf("b = %d | lambda1 = %.4f, lambda2 = %.4f, BIC = %.2f\n",
            b, grid_b$best$lambda1, grid_b$best$lambda2, grid_b$best$bic))
cat(sprintf("MSE(observed, truth): %.4f\n", mean((y_b - truth_vec)^2)))
cat(sprintf("MSE(beta_hat, truth): %.4f\n", mean((beta_b - truth_vec)^2)))
```

```{r}
# Sanity check: does snapping give exactly identical values to fused pixels?
# Sanity check on the dry-run replication (b = 1): a strict != comparison and one with
# tolerance 1e-6 must both return 0, so no numerical residuals are mistaken for changes.

B_chk <- matrix(beta_b, ncol = T_sim)
sum(B_chk[, 2] != B_chk[, 1])                 # strict
sum(abs(B_chk[, 2] - B_chk[, 1]) > 1e-6)      # with tolerance
```

```{r}
# Sanity check: does snapping give exactly identical values to fused pixels?
# Sanity check on the dry-run replication (b = 1): a strict != comparison and one with
# tolerance 1e-6 must return the same count, so no numerical residuals are mistaken for changes.
# The count itself does not need to be zero: it is the number of pixels with a false change
# between Q1 and Q2 (identical true signal), a statistical result that depends on the
# strength of the regularization.

B_chk <- matrix(beta_b, ncol = T_sim)
n_strict <- sum(B_chk[, 2] != B_chk[, 1]); n_tol <- sum(abs(B_chk[, 2] - B_chk[, 1]) > 1e-6)
stopifnot(n_strict == n_tol)                      # snapping: no numerical residuals
c(false_change_pixels_Q1_Q2 = n_tol)              # statistical result, not an error
```

### Monte Carlo Loop

In each replication, fresh Gaussian noise is added to the fixed ground truth, lambda is selected by BIC on the full grid, and the ADMM fit is snapped to clusters. For each replication we store the overall MSE, the selected lambdas, and the following metrics.

**MSE of the temporal differences.** The MSE of the differences between consecutive quarters (Q2 - Q1 and Q3 - Q2), computed for both the observed data and the estimate against the true differences. The observed data serve as a baseline: no model, just the noisy differences.

**Change detection.** For each transition, a pixel is flagged as "changed" if its value differs between the two quarters. Accuracy is the share of pixels where the estimated flag matches the true one. True positives (true changes detected), false positives (changes found where there are none) and false negatives (true changes missed) are counted separately, since accuracy alone is dominated by the large number of unchanged pixels.

**Cluster recovery.** The Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) compares the estimated partition of the space-time pixels with the true one, defined as the connected components of neighboring pixels with equal true value (the best partition the fused lasso can recover, since it only fuses neighbors). 1 means identical partitions. The number of estimated clusters is stored too, and the ARI is repeated quarter by quarter on the purely spatial partition.

**Center block.** The mean estimate over the 4 pixels of the center block in each quarter, to quantify how much of the true jump (3 -\> 5) is recovered.

True partitions used as reference for the ARI, built once outside the loop. Since the fused lasso only fuses pixels connected by an edge, the reference is not the partition by value but the connected components of equal true value: the 4 neighbor blocks of the plus are not adjacent to each other, so they count as 4 separate clusters (8 clusters in total). The second partition uses only spatial edges, to compare clusters quarter by quarter (7 per quarter).

```{r}
# True partition: connected components of pixels with equal true value
# (what the fused lasso can recover at best, since it only fuses neighboring pixels)
Dt    <- as(rbind(D_space_sim, D_time_sim), "TsparseMatrix")
pairs <- do.call(rbind, tapply(Dt@j, Dt@i, function(v) v + 1))   # each row of D has 2 nonzeros
same  <- truth_vec[pairs[, 1]] == truth_vec[pairs[, 2]]

g    <- make_empty_graph(n = length(truth_vec), directed = FALSE)
g    <- add_edges(g, as.vector(t(pairs[same, ])))
comp <- components(g)$membership

cat("Number of true connected clusters:", max(comp), "\n")   # expected: 8
```

```{r}
# True spatial partition: connected components using only spatial edges (no temporal links),
# so that clusters can be compared quarter by quarter
Ds     <- as(D_space_sim, "TsparseMatrix")
pairs_s <- do.call(rbind, tapply(Ds@j, Ds@i, function(v) v + 1))
same_s  <- truth_vec[pairs_s[, 1]] == truth_vec[pairs_s[, 2]]

g_s        <- make_empty_graph(n = length(truth_vec), directed = FALSE)
g_s        <- add_edges(g_s, as.vector(t(pairs_s[same_s, ])))
comp_space <- components(g_s)$membership

# Pixel indices of each quarter (the vector is ordered layer by layer)
idx_q <- lapply(1:T_sim, function(t) ((t - 1) * n_cells_sim + 1):(t * n_cells_sim))

cat("True spatial clusters per quarter:",
    sapply(idx_q, function(i) length(unique(comp_space[i]))), "\n")   # expected: 7 7 7
```

```{r}
res <- vector("list", B)

system.time(
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # Replication-specific seed: each replication draws its own independent noise,
    # and any single replication b can be reproduced on its own by re-running set.seed(1000 + b).
    set.seed(1000 + b)
    y_b <- as.vector(truth_vec + rnorm(length(truth_vec), 0, sigma_sim))
    
    grid_b <- grid_search_lambda(y = y_b, dims = dims_t1, 
                                 D_space = D_space_sim, D_time = D_time_sim,
                                 lambda1_grid = lambda1_grid_sim,
                                 lambda2_grid = lambda2_grid_sim, n_cores = 1)
    
    ops_b <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space_sim, D_time_sim, n = length(y_b), rho = 1)
    fit_b <- admm_fusedlasso3d(y = y_b, ops = ops_b,
                               lambda1 = grid_b$best$lambda1,
                               lambda2 = grid_b$best$lambda2,
                               max_iter = 500, verbose = FALSE)
    beta_b <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit_b$beta, fit_b$z1, fit_b$z2,
                                    edge_pairs_space_sim, edge_pairs_time_sim,
                                    n = length(y_b))
    
    # cells x quarters matrices
    Y_b  <- matrix(y_b,        ncol = T_sim)
    B_b  <- matrix(beta_b,     ncol = T_sim)
    Tr_b <- matrix(truth_vec,  ncol = T_sim)
    
    # Snapping invariant used by detect(): the strict and the tolerance-based change flags must coincide,
    # otherwise numerical residuals would be counted as changes (false positives)
    for (t in 1:(T_sim - 1)) {
      stopifnot(sum(B_b[, t + 1] != B_b[, t]) == sum(abs(B_b[, t + 1] - B_b[, t]) > 1e-6))
    }
    
    # MSE of a temporal difference (layer t+1 minus layer t) against the true difference
    mse_diff <- function(M, t) mean(((M[, t + 1] - M[, t]) - (Tr_b[, t + 1] - Tr_b[, t]))^2)
    
    # Change detection between layer t and t+1: estimated flag vs true flag, pixel by pixel
    detect <- function(M, t) {
      est  <- M[, t + 1] != M[, t]
      true <- Tr_b[, t + 1] != Tr_b[, t]
      c(acc = mean(est == true), tp = sum(est & true), fp = sum(est & !true), fn = sum(!est & true))
    }
    det12 <- detect(B_b, 1)
    det23 <- detect(B_b, 2)
    
    # Mean estimate over the center block (pixels whose true value changes at Q3) in each quarter
    center_cells <- which(Tr_b[, 3] != Tr_b[, 2])
    center_est   <- colMeans(B_b[center_cells, , drop = FALSE])
    
    # Compute Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between the true and the estimated partition of the space-time pixels
    # (true partition = connected components of equal true value, `comp`, built once outside the loop)
    ari_val <- adjustedRandIndex(comp, round(beta_b, 8))
    
    # ARI quarter by quarter (spatial partition only)
    ari_q <- sapply(1:T_sim, function(t)
      adjustedRandIndex(comp_space[idx_q[[t]]], round(beta_b[idx_q[[t]]], 8)))
    
    res[[b]] <- data.frame(b = b,
                           mse_obs      = mean((y_b - truth_vec)^2),
                           mse_beta     = mean((beta_b - truth_vec)^2),
                           mse_obs_d12  = mse_diff(Y_b, 1),
                           mse_beta_d12 = mse_diff(B_b, 1),
                           mse_obs_d23  = mse_diff(Y_b, 2),
                           mse_beta_d23 = mse_diff(B_b, 2),
                           acc_d12 = det12["acc"], fp_d12 = det12["fp"],
                           acc_d23 = det23["acc"], tp_d23 = det23["tp"], fp_d23 = det23["fp"], fn_d23 = det23["fn"],
                           ari          = ari_val,
                           ari_q1 = ari_q[1], ari_q2 = ari_q[2], ari_q3 = ari_q[3],
                           center_q1 = center_est[1], center_q2 = center_est[2], center_q3 = center_est[3],
                           n_clusters   = length(unique(round(beta_b, 8))),
                           lambda1      = grid_b$best$lambda1,
                           lambda2      = grid_b$best$lambda2,
                           sigma2_est   = grid_b$sigma2_est,       # noise variance estimate (true value: sigma_sim^2 = 0.04)
                           n_iter       = fit_b$n_iter,            # must be < 500, otherwise the final fit did not converge
                           # optimum at a grid boundary (lambda = 0, smallest positive value, or largest value)
                           edge_l1 = grid_b$best$lambda1 %in% c(0, min(lambda1_grid_sim[lambda1_grid_sim > 0]), max(lambda1_grid_sim)),
                           edge_l2 = grid_b$best$lambda2 %in% c(0, min(lambda2_grid_sim[lambda2_grid_sim > 0]), max(lambda2_grid_sim)))
  }
)

res <- do.call(rbind, res)
head(res)
```

```{r}
# Post-loop checks
summary(res$n_iter)                                  # the maximum must stay below 500
colMeans(res[, c("edge_l1", "edge_l2")])             # should be close to 0; otherwise widen the grid
c(sigma2_mean = mean(res$sigma2_est), true = sigma_sim^2)
```

Visualization of a single replication: ground truth (top row), noisy observed data (middle row) and fused lasso estimate (bottom row), on the same color scale. The replication is re-fitted using the lambdas selected during the Monte Carlo loop.

```{r}
b_show <- 1
# change to 3 to inspect the replication where the estimate is worse than the raw data

## Regenerate the noise of replication b_show and refit with its selected lambdas
set.seed(1000 + b_show)
y_show <- as.vector(truth_vec + rnorm(length(truth_vec), 0, sigma_sim))

ops_show <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space_sim, D_time_sim, n = length(y_show), rho = 1)
fit_show <- admm_fusedlasso3d(y = y_show, ops = ops_show,
                              lambda1 = res$lambda1[b_show],
                              lambda2 = res$lambda2[b_show],
                              max_iter = 500, verbose = FALSE)
beta_show <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit_show$beta, fit_show$z1, fit_show$z2,
                                   edge_pairs_space_sim, edge_pairs_time_sim,
                                   n = length(y_show))

cat(sprintf("b = %d | MSE(obs) = %.4f, MSE(beta) = %.4f (from res: %.4f, %.4f)\n",
            b_show, mean((y_show - truth_vec)^2), mean((beta_show - truth_vec)^2),
            res$mse_obs[b_show], res$mse_beta[b_show]))

## Build observed and estimated stacks
r_stack_obs_show <- r_stack_truth
values(r_stack_obs_show) <- matrix(y_show, ncol = T_sim)
names(r_stack_obs_show) <- names(r_stack_truth)

r_stack_est_show <- r_stack_truth
values(r_stack_est_show) <- matrix(beta_show, ncol = T_sim)

zlim_full[1] <- zlim_full[1] - 1e-6
zlim_full[2] <- zlim_full[2] + 1e-6
```

### Center Block

```{r}
summary(res[, c("center_q1", "center_q2", "center_q3")])

```

```{r}
# Predicted shrinkage of the center block if the cluster is recovered exactly:
# bias = (sum of lambda x boundary edges, signed) / cluster size
# Q3 (4 pixels): 8 spatial + 4 temporal edges, all pushing down      -> 2*l1 + l2
# Q1/Q2 (8 pixels): 16 spatial edges pushing down, 4 temporal up     -> 2*l1 - l2/2
res$bias_q3_obs   <- 5 - res$center_q3
res$bias_q12_obs  <- 3 - (res$center_q1 + res$center_q2) / 2
res$bias_q3_pred  <- 2 * res$lambda1 + res$lambda2
res$bias_q12_pred <- 2 * res$lambda1 - res$lambda2 / 2

cat(sprintf("Q3:    observed = %.3f, predicted = %.3f, cor = %.3f, slope = %.2f\n",
            mean(res$bias_q3_obs), mean(res$bias_q3_pred),
            cor(res$bias_q3_obs, res$bias_q3_pred),
            coef(lm(bias_q3_obs ~ bias_q3_pred, data = res))[2]))
cat(sprintf("Q1/Q2: observed = %.3f, predicted = %.3f, cor = %.3f, slope = %.2f\n",
            mean(res$bias_q12_obs), mean(res$bias_q12_pred),
            cor(res$bias_q12_obs, res$bias_q12_pred),
            coef(lm(bias_q12_obs ~ bias_q12_pred, data = res))[2]))
```

## TEST 2: Multiple Independent Clusters with Distinct Temporal Trajectories

Simulation: 16x16 grid, 2x2 constant blocks, 3 quarters, B = 30 Monte Carlo replications.

Ground truth: three non-adjacent 2x2 blocks placed well inside the grid (away from edges and corners, to avoid confounding boundary effects with cluster-distinguishing behavior), each following a different temporal pattern over a constant background (value 1): gradual growth (cluster A: 2 -\> 3 -\> 4), stable (cluster B: 3 -\> 3 -\> 3) and sudden decline (cluster C: 4 -\> 4 -\> 2). The ground truth is fixed across replications; in each replication, independent iid Gaussian noise (sd = 0.2) is added to it.

```{r}
nrow_sim_t2   <- 16
ncol_sim_t2   <- 16
block_size_t2 <- 2
n_blocks_t2   <- nrow_sim_t2 / block_size_t2   # 8x8 blocks

sigma_sim_t2  <- 0.2                           # noise sd
B_t2          <- 30                            # number of Monte Carlo replications

background_val_t2 <- 1
```

Ground truth block values per quarter (8x8 block grid)

- Cluster A (block 3,3): gradual GROWTH 2 -\> 3 -\> 4

- Cluster B (block 3,6): STABLE 3 -\> 3 -\> 3

- Cluster C (block 6,3): sudden DECLINE 4 -\> 4 -\> 2

All three blocks sit well inside the grid (rows/cols 2-7 out of 1-8), at least 2 blocks apart from each other and from the edge.

```{r}
## Ground truth block values per quarter (8x8 block grid)
block_vals_t2_q1 <- matrix(background_val_t2, nrow = n_blocks_t2, ncol = n_blocks_t2)
block_vals_t2_q1[3, 3] <- 2   # cluster A, Q1
block_vals_t2_q1[3, 6] <- 3   # cluster B, Q1
block_vals_t2_q1[6, 3] <- 4   # cluster C, Q1

block_vals_t2_q2 <- block_vals_t2_q1
block_vals_t2_q2[3, 3] <- 3   # cluster A, Q2 (growing)
block_vals_t2_q2[3, 6] <- 3   # cluster B, Q2 (stable)
block_vals_t2_q2[6, 3] <- 4   # cluster C, Q2 (not yet changed)

block_vals_t2_q3 <- block_vals_t2_q2
block_vals_t2_q3[3, 3] <- 4   # cluster A, Q3 (further growth)
block_vals_t2_q3[3, 6] <- 3   # cluster B, Q3 (stable)
block_vals_t2_q3[6, 3] <- 2   # cluster C, Q3 (sudden decline)

## Expand to full 16x16 pixel grids
truth_t2_q1 <- expand_blocks(block_vals_t2_q1, block_size_t2)
truth_t2_q2 <- expand_blocks(block_vals_t2_q2, block_size_t2)
truth_t2_q3 <- expand_blocks(block_vals_t2_q3, block_size_t2)
```

```{r}
dim(truth_t2_q3)
table(truth_t2_q3)
```

Build the ground truth as a SpatRaster stack, so it plugs directly into the same `build_spatial_D()` / `build_temporal_D()` pipeline used on the real Kampala data. Observed stacks are not built here: noise is generated inside each replication.

```{r}
r_stack_truth_t2 <- rast(list(rast(truth_t2_q1), rast(truth_t2_q2), rast(truth_t2_q3)))
names(r_stack_truth_t2) <- c("Sim Q1", "Sim Q2", "Sim Q3")
```

Visualization: ground truth (top row) vs one example of noisy observed data (bottom row, same noise as replication b = 1), on the same color scale across all six panels for a fair comparison.

```{r}
## Example of noisy data (same noise as replication b = 1), for illustration only
truth_vec_t2 <- as.vector(terra::values(r_stack_truth_t2))

set.seed(1000 + 1)
y_example_t2 <- truth_vec_t2 + rnorm(length(truth_vec_t2), mean = 0, sd = sigma_sim_t2)

r_stack_example_t2 <- r_stack_truth_t2
values(r_stack_example_t2) <- matrix(y_example_t2, ncol = terra::nlyr(r_stack_truth_t2))
names(r_stack_example_t2) <- names(r_stack_truth_t2)

## Same color scale across all panels
zlim_sim_t2 <- range(c(values(r_stack_truth_t2), values(r_stack_example_t2)), na.rm = TRUE)
zlim_sim_t2[2] <- zlim_sim_t2[2] + 1e-6

par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
for (t in 1:3) {
  plot(r_stack_truth_t2[[t]], main = paste("Truth -", names(r_stack_truth_t2)[t]),
       range = zlim_sim_t2, type = "continuous")
}
for (t in 1:3) {
  plot(r_stack_example_t2[[t]], main = paste("Observed (example) -", names(r_stack_example_t2)[t]),
       range = zlim_sim_t2, type = "continuous")
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Extract the spatial/temporal dimensions and build the penalty matrices once, outside the replication loop: they depend only on the grid geometry, not on the noise. The same functions as in Part 2 (real data) are reused.

```{r}
nrow_sim_t2_k  <- terra::nrow(r_stack_truth_t2)
ncol_sim_t2_k  <- terra::ncol(r_stack_truth_t2)
n_cells_sim_t2 <- terra::ncell(r_stack_truth_t2)
T_sim_t2       <- terra::nlyr(r_stack_truth_t2)

# Dimensions vector for tensor-based variance estimation (Option 2)
dims_t2 <- c(nrow_sim_t2_k, ncol_sim_t2_k, T_sim_t2)

## Penalty matrices (built once, shared by all replications)
D_space_t2 <- build_spatial_D(r_stack_truth_t2, nrow_sim_t2_k, ncol_sim_t2_k, n_cells_sim_t2, T_sim_t2)
D_time_t2  <- build_temporal_D(n_cells_sim_t2, T_sim_t2)

cat(sprintf("Simulation built: %d x %d grid, %d quarters, noise sd = %.2f, B = %d\n",
            nrow_sim_t2_k, ncol_sim_t2_k, T_sim_t2, sigma_sim_t2, B_t2))
cat(sprintf("D_space: %d x %d, D_time: %d x %d\n",
            nrow(D_space_t2), ncol(D_space_t2), nrow(D_time_t2), ncol(D_time_t2)))
```

Lambda grids and edge pairs, also built once outside the replication loop. Lambda grids span 1e-4 to 1 (15 values each), the same range as Test 1. The edge pairs are needed by `snap_beta_to_clusters()` and depend only on the penalty matrices.

```{r}
## Lambda grids (searched afresh in every replication)
lambda1_grid_t2 <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = 1e-4, max_val = 1, n = 15)
lambda2_grid_t2 <- build_lambda_grid(min_val = 1e-4, max_val = 1, n = 15)

## Edge pairs for the snapping step (depend only on D, not on the noise)
edge_pairs_space_t2 <- get_edge_pairs(D_space_t2)
edge_pairs_time_t2  <- get_edge_pairs(D_time_t2)

cat(sprintf("Lambda grid: %d x %d = %d combinations per replication\n",
            length(lambda1_grid_t2), length(lambda2_grid_t2),
            length(lambda1_grid_t2) * length(lambda2_grid_t2)))
```

Dry run on a single replication (b = 1) to check the pipeline and measure the runtime before launching all B replications. The grid has 4 times more pixels than Test 1, so expect a longer runtime per replication.

```{r}
b <- 1

system.time({
  set.seed(1000 + b)
  y_b <- as.vector(truth_vec_t2 + rnorm(length(truth_vec_t2), 0, sigma_sim_t2))
  
  grid_b <- grid_search_lambda(y = y_b, dims = dims_t2,
                               D_space = D_space_t2, D_time = D_time_t2,
                               lambda1_grid = lambda1_grid_t2,
                               lambda2_grid = lambda2_grid_t2, n_cores = 1)
  
  ops_b <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space_t2, D_time_t2, n = length(y_b), rho = 1)
  fit_b <- admm_fusedlasso3d(y = y_b, ops = ops_b,
                             lambda1 = grid_b$best$lambda1,
                             lambda2 = grid_b$best$lambda2, max_iter = 500)
  beta_b <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit_b$beta, fit_b$z1, fit_b$z2,
                                  edge_pairs_space_t2, edge_pairs_time_t2,
                                  n = length(y_b))
})

cat(sprintf("b = %d | lambda1 = %.4f, lambda2 = %.4f, BIC = %.2f\n",
            b, grid_b$best$lambda1, grid_b$best$lambda2, grid_b$best$bic))
cat(sprintf("MSE(observed, truth): %.4f\n", mean((y_b - truth_vec_t2)^2)))
cat(sprintf("MSE(beta_hat, truth): %.4f\n", mean((beta_b - truth_vec_t2)^2)))
```

Sanity check: does snapping give exactly identical values to fused pixels? On the dry-run replication (b = 1), a strict `!=` comparison and one with tolerance 1e-6 must both return the same count, so no numerical residuals are mistaken for changes. Unlike Test 1, here the counts are not expected to be 0 for Q1 -\> Q2 or Q2 -\> Q3, since the true changes are not zero. The expected number of true changes is 4 (Q1 -\> Q2, cluster A) and 8 (Q2 -\> Q3, clusters A and C).

```{r}
B_chk <- matrix(beta_b, ncol = T_sim_t2)

# Q1 -> Q2 (expected: 4 true changes, cluster A)
sum(B_chk[, 2] != B_chk[, 1])                 # strict
sum(abs(B_chk[, 2] - B_chk[, 1]) > 1e-6)      # with tolerance

# Q2 -> Q3 (expected: 8 true changes, clusters A and C)
sum(B_chk[, 3] != B_chk[, 2])                 # strict
sum(abs(B_chk[, 3] - B_chk[, 2]) > 1e-6)      # with tolerance
```

True partitions used as reference for the ARI, built once outside the loop. Since the fused lasso only fuses pixels connected by an edge, the reference is not the partition by value but the connected components of equal true value. The first partition uses spatial and temporal edges: the background is one cluster connected across all quarters, cluster B is one cluster (stable), cluster A splits into 3 clusters (a different value in each quarter), and cluster C into 2 (value 4 over Q1-Q2, value 2 at Q3), for 7 clusters in total.

```{r}
# True partition: connected components of pixels with equal true value
# (what the fused lasso can recover at best, since it only fuses neighboring pixels)
Dt    <- as(rbind(D_space_t2, D_time_t2), "TsparseMatrix")
pairs <- do.call(rbind, tapply(Dt@j, Dt@i, function(v) v + 1))   # each row of D has 2 nonzeros
same  <- truth_vec_t2[pairs[, 1]] == truth_vec_t2[pairs[, 2]]

g    <- make_empty_graph(n = length(truth_vec_t2), directed = FALSE)
g    <- add_edges(g, as.vector(t(pairs[same, ])))
comp <- components(g)$membership

cat("Number of true connected clusters:", max(comp), "\n")   # expected: 7
```

The second partition uses only spatial edges, to compare clusters quarter by quarter: in each quarter there are 4 clusters (the background and the three blocks).

```{r}
# True spatial partition: connected components using only spatial edges (no temporal links),
# so that clusters can be compared quarter by quarter
Ds      <- as(D_space_t2, "TsparseMatrix")
pairs_s <- do.call(rbind, tapply(Ds@j, Ds@i, function(v) v + 1))
same_s  <- truth_vec_t2[pairs_s[, 1]] == truth_vec_t2[pairs_s[, 2]]

g_s        <- make_empty_graph(n = length(truth_vec_t2), directed = FALSE)
g_s        <- add_edges(g_s, as.vector(t(pairs_s[same_s, ])))
comp_space <- components(g_s)$membership

# Pixel indices of each quarter (the vector is ordered layer by layer)
idx_q <- lapply(1:T_sim_t2, function(t) ((t - 1) * n_cells_sim_t2 + 1):(t * n_cells_sim_t2))

cat("True spatial clusters per quarter:",
    sapply(idx_q, function(i) length(unique(comp_space[i]))), "\n")   # expected: 4 4 4
```

The cluster masks are defined by block position, not by value, so they stay valid even if two clusters share a value in some quarter. They are built in terra cell order (row by row), so they can be applied directly to the cells x quarters matrices used inside the loop.

```{r}
mask_block <- function(i, j) {
  m <- matrix(FALSE, n_blocks_t2, n_blocks_t2)
  m[i, j] <- TRUE
  as.vector(t(expand_blocks(m, block_size_t2)))   # t(): terra cell order is row by row
}

mask_list <- list(growth  = mask_block(3, 3),   # cluster A
                  stable  = mask_block(3, 6),   # cluster B
                  decline = mask_block(6, 3))   # cluster C
mask_list$bg <- !(mask_list$growth | mask_list$stable | mask_list$decline)
cl_names <- names(mask_list)

sapply(mask_list, sum)   # expected: growth 4, stable 4, decline 4, bg 244
```

Helper functions for the per-replication metrics, also defined once. They compute the MSE of a temporal difference against the true difference, the change detection counts (overall and for the growth and decline clusters), and the MSE / mean estimate by cluster and quarter.

```{r}
Tr_t2 <- matrix(truth_vec_t2, ncol = T_sim_t2)   # cells x quarters

# MSE of a temporal difference (layer t+1 minus layer t) against the true difference
mse_diff <- function(M, t) mean(((M[, t + 1] - M[, t]) - (Tr_t2[, t + 1] - Tr_t2[, t]))^2)

# Change detection between layer t and t+1: estimated flag vs true flag, pixel by pixel
# (true positives are also counted separately for the growth and decline clusters)
detect <- function(M, t) {
  est  <- M[, t + 1] != M[, t]
  true <- Tr_t2[, t + 1] != Tr_t2[, t]
  c(acc = mean(est == true), tp = sum(est & true), fp = sum(est & !true), fn = sum(!est & true),
    tp_growth  = sum(est & true & mask_list$growth),
    tp_decline = sum(est & true & mask_list$decline))
}

# Statistic by cluster and quarter, flattened into a named list (e.g. mse_growth_q1)
cl_stat <- function(M, fun, prefix) {
  out <- sapply(mask_list, function(m)
    sapply(1:T_sim_t2, function(t) fun(M[m, t], Tr_t2[m, t])))
  nm  <- outer(1:T_sim_t2, cl_names, function(t, cl) paste0(prefix, "_", cl, "_q", t))
  setNames(as.list(as.vector(out)), as.vector(nm))
}
```

### Monte Carlo Loop

Monte Carlo loop. In each replication, fresh Gaussian noise is added to the fixed ground truth, lambda is selected by BIC on the full grid, and the ADMM fit is snapped to clusters. For each replication we store the overall MSE, the selected lambdas, and the following metrics.

- **MSE of the temporal differences.** The MSE of the differences between consecutive quarters (Q2 - Q1 and Q3 - Q2), for both the observed data and the estimate, against the true differences. The observed data serve as a baseline.

- **Change detection.** For each transition, a pixel is flagged as “changed” if its value differs between the two quarters. We store accuracy, true positives, false positives and false negatives. True positives are also counted separately for the growth cluster (Q1 -\> Q2 and Q2 -\> Q3) and the decline cluster (Q2 -\> Q3). The true changes are 4 pixels in Q1 -\> Q2 and 8 in Q2 -\> Q3.

- **Cluster recovery.** The ARI between the estimated and the true space-time partition, the ARI quarter by quarter on the spatial partition, and the number of estimated clusters.

- **By cluster and quarter.** The MSE and the mean estimate of each cluster (growth, stable, decline, background) in each quarter, to quantify how much of each trajectory is recovered.

```{r}
res <- vector("list", B_t2)

system.time(
  for (b in seq_len(B_t2)) {
    # Replication-specific seed: each replication draws its own independent noise,
    # and any single replication b can be reproduced on its own by re-running set.seed(1000 + b).
    set.seed(1000 + b)
    y_b <- as.vector(truth_vec_t2 + rnorm(length(truth_vec_t2), 0, sigma_sim_t2))
    
    grid_b <- grid_search_lambda(y = y_b, dims = dims_t2,
                                 D_space = D_space_t2, D_time = D_time_t2,
                                 lambda1_grid = lambda1_grid_t2,
                                 lambda2_grid = lambda2_grid_t2, n_cores = 1)
    
    ops_b <- prepare_admm_operators(D_space_t2, D_time_t2, n = length(y_b), rho = 1)
    fit_b <- admm_fusedlasso3d(y = y_b, ops = ops_b,
                               lambda1 = grid_b$best$lambda1,
                               lambda2 = grid_b$best$lambda2,
                               max_iter = 500, verbose = FALSE)
    beta_b <- snap_beta_to_clusters(fit_b$beta, fit_b$z1, fit_b$z2,
                                    edge_pairs_space_t2, edge_pairs_time_t2,
                                    n = length(y_b))
    
    # cells x quarters matrices
    Y_b <- matrix(y_b,    ncol = T_sim_t2)
    B_b <- matrix(beta_b, ncol = T_sim_t2)
    
    # Snapping invariant used by detect(): the strict and the tolerance-based change flags must coincide,
    # otherwise numerical residuals would be counted as changes (false positives)
    for (t in 1:(T_sim_t2 - 1)) {
      stopifnot(sum(B_b[, t + 1] != B_b[, t]) == sum(abs(B_b[, t + 1] - B_b[, t]) > 1e-6))
    }
    
    det12 <- detect(B_b, 1)
    det23 <- detect(B_b, 2)
    
    # ARI between the true and the estimated partition of the space-time pixels
    ari_val <- adjustedRandIndex(comp, round(beta_b, 8))
    
    # ARI quarter by quarter (spatial partition only)
    ari_q <- sapply(1:T_sim_t2, function(t)
      adjustedRandIndex(comp_space[idx_q[[t]]], round(beta_b[idx_q[[t]]], 8)))
    
    res[[b]] <- data.frame(
      b = b,
      mse_obs      = mean((y_b - truth_vec_t2)^2),
      mse_beta     = mean((beta_b - truth_vec_t2)^2),
      mse_obs_d12  = mse_diff(Y_b, 1), mse_beta_d12 = mse_diff(B_b, 1),
      mse_obs_d23  = mse_diff(Y_b, 2), mse_beta_d23 = mse_diff(B_b, 2),
      acc_d12 = det12["acc"], tp_d12 = det12["tp"], fp_d12 = det12["fp"], fn_d12 = det12["fn"],
      tp_growth_d12 = det12["tp_growth"],
      acc_d23 = det23["acc"], tp_d23 = det23["tp"], fp_d23 = det23["fp"], fn_d23 = det23["fn"],
      tp_growth_d23 = det23["tp_growth"], tp_decline_d23 = det23["tp_decline"],
      ari = ari_val, ari_q1 = ari_q[1], ari_q2 = ari_q[2], ari_q3 = ari_q[3],
      cl_stat(B_b, function(e, tr) mean((e - tr)^2), "mse"),   # MSE by cluster and quarter
      cl_stat(B_b, function(e, tr) mean(e),          "est"),   # mean estimate by cluster and quarter
      n_clusters   = length(unique(round(beta_b, 8))),
      lambda1      = grid_b$best$lambda1,
      lambda2      = grid_b$best$lambda2,
      sigma2_est   = grid_b$sigma2_est,       # noise variance estimate (true value: sigma_sim_t2^2)
      n_iter       = fit_b$n_iter,            # must be < 500, otherwise the final fit did not converge
      # optimum at a grid boundary (lambda = 0, smallest positive value, or largest value)
      edge_l1 = grid_b$best$lambda1 %in% c(0, min(lambda1_grid_t2[lambda1_grid_t2 > 0]), max(lambda1_grid_t2)),
      edge_l2 = grid_b$best$lambda2 %in% c(0, min(lambda2_grid_t2[lambda2_grid_t2 > 0]), max(lambda2_grid_t2)),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }
)

res <- do.call(rbind, res)
head(res)
```

```{r}
# Post-loop checks
summary(res$n_iter)                                  # the maximum must stay below 500
colMeans(res[, c("edge_l1", "edge_l2")])             # should be close to 0; otherwise widen the grid
c(sigma2_mean = mean(res$sigma2_est), true = sigma_sim_t2^2)
```

Visualization of a single replication: ground truth (top row), noisy observed data (middle row) and fused lasso estimate (bottom row), on the same color scale. The replication is re-fitted using the lambdas selected during the Monte Carlo loop. Change `b_show` to inspect other replications, for example the one where the estimate is worst.

```{r}
res$ari[1]
```

```{r}
b_show <- 1
```
